task_title: Phase P04 — Generalized lesson resources and video

workstreams.title: Data model and zero-loss migration
steps: Introduce LessonResource as the canonical entity with a resource-type discriminator for Video, Image, Document, Link, and Attachment; retain every existing ContentLessonVideo identifier and metadata field.

Prefer an in-place compatibility mapping over destructive replacement: preserve the existing table and primary keys while adding nullable resource fields, archive state, ordering, workflow metadata, and SQL Server RowVersion. If the architecture requires a table rename, use EF rename operations rather than drop/recreate.
Set existing rows deterministically to resource type Video and derive only values already represented by existing metadata; do not invent URLs, providers, thumbnails, durations, or placeholder rows.
Add indexes and constraints for lesson/order, workflow visibility, and archived filtering. Keep lesson-resource relationships optional and avoid a minimum-resource constraint.
Review generated Up and Down operations manually for destructive SQL. Produce a migration script for controlled maintenance, but do not apply it to StudyAIDb during automated work.

workstreams.title: Resource validation, workflow, concurrency, and audit
steps: Centralize create, update, reorder, archive, verify, reject, publish, and unpublish behavior in a LessonResource service; retain a temporary ContentVideosService compatibility facade where existing callers require it.

Define explicit workflow transitions: authors manage draft/rejected resources; reviewers verify or reject; only authorized reviewers publish or unpublish; published resources must be unpublished before content mutation or archival.

Require RowVersion on update, reorder, archive, and workflow commands. Translate EF concurrency failures and stale versions into HTTP 409 responses containing the current representation/version without silently overwriting data.

Validate type-specific metadata and absolute URLs. Permit only configured http/https behavior, enforce provider/host allowlists for embeddable media, reject credentials, malformed hosts, javascript:, data:, file:, loopback, link-local, private/reserved IP destinations, unsafe redirects, and disallowed ports.

Avoid server-side URL fetching unless explicitly required. If probing is required, repeat DNS/IP and redirect validation at every hop with strict time and size limits to prevent SSRF or DNS rebinding.

Write StaffAuditLog entries for create/update/reorder/archive and every verification/publish transition, including actor, resource and lesson IDs, before/after state, timestamp, and safe reason metadata; never log secrets or private student data.

workstreams.title: RBAC and API compatibility
steps: Expose lesson-scoped resource list/create plus resource-scoped update, reorder, archive, verify, reject, publish, and unpublish endpoints using existing API conventions.

Require authentication for all management endpoints. Restrict draft CRUD/reorder/archive to ContentAuthor and approved staff roles, and verification/publishing transitions to the configured reviewer/admin policy.
Enforce lesson/resource relationship checks and author ownership or assigned-scope rules before mutation; return 404 or 403 consistently without leaking inaccessible resource details.

Preserve existing video endpoint contracts during frontend migration by routing them through the generalized service and retaining existing ContentLessonVideo IDs; document any compatibility deprecation rather than breaking consumers.
Return validation errors as 400, unauthenticated as 401, unauthorized as 403, missing resources as 404, and stale RowVersion as 409. Never return success when persistence or audit logging fails.

workstreams.title: Learner-safe resource projection
steps: Replace the video-only learner projection with an ordered resource projection while retaining compatibility fields needed by the current LessonVideoPlayer during rollout.
Project only published, verified, non-archived resources belonging to lessons the learner may access; never expose draft workflow fields, audit metadata, or internal storage details.
Return an empty resource collection for lessons without media. Do not synthesize placeholder resources or fake URLs.
Handle legacy or invalid video rows safely: omit unsafe/unrenderable media or expose a non-success display state without crashing the lesson page, while preserving valid lesson text.
Add projection tests for ordering, type mapping, no-resource lessons, invalid legacy video data, unpublished/archived exclusion, and learner isolation.

workstreams.title: Content management UI
steps: Add a pragmatic resource section to ContentLessonEditorPage using existing form, list, dialog, status, and notification components.
Support resource type selection, type-specific fields, create/edit, deterministic reorder, archive confirmation, verify/reject, publish/unpublish, and visible workflow status.
Send RowVersion with every mutation. On 409, retain unsaved user input, display a clear conflict message, and offer reload/retry rather than claiming success.
Show explicit loading, empty, validation, permission, API failure, and success states; show success only after the server confirms persistence.
Keep the UI keyboard accessible, readable at 390px, and consistent with existing tokens. Do not add placeholder media, fake URLs, or optimistic state that survives a failed API request.

workstreams.title: Learner LessonPage rendering
steps: Render ordered published resources on LessonPage with type-appropriate presentation: safe video player, image, document/attachment download link, and external link.
Reuse LessonVideoPlayer for supported providers, but fail visibly and safely for invalid or unsupported video URLs without preventing access to lesson content.
Use safe link attributes and avoid injecting provider HTML. Do not embed arbitrary origins or trust frontend-only URL validation.
Treat resources as optional: the lesson remains fully usable when the resource collection is empty.
Add component tests for every resource type, ordering, empty state, invalid video, API failure, accessibility, and mobile layout.

workstreams.title: Automated verification and regressions
steps: Add unit tests for type validation, provider/URL policy, SSRF cases, state transitions, RBAC decisions, RowVersion conflicts, ordering, archival, audit generation, and optional-resource behavior.

Run integration tests only with Testing configuration and a per-run StudyAIDb_Clean_{GUID} database created and owned by the test harness. Verify the resolved database name before provisioning and abort if it is StudyAIDb, StudyAIDb_E2E, StudyAIDb_Dev, or any nonconforming name.

Add Playwright coverage for CRUD, reorder, archive, verify/publish, URL rejection, no-video lesson, invalid video, 401, 403, 409 conflict recovery, refresh persistence, two-user isolation, API failure, and 390px mobile behavior.

Run affected P02/P03 regression suites plus frontend lint/test/build and backend restore/build/test gates. Summarize logs into TEST-SUMMARY.json and report unavailable gates as NOT RUN rather than PASS.

Inspect the migration against a disposable clean database and a disposable snapshot containing representative legacy ContentLessonVideo rows; assert IDs, metadata, relationships, and row counts survive migration.
Request read-only Codex review after tests, remediate blocking findings within the permitted attempts, and update PROGRESS.md with evidence and unresolved risks.

acceptance_criteria: All pre-existing ContentLessonVideo rows retain their IDs, lesson relationships, URLs, provider metadata, titles/captions, ordering, and other stored metadata after migration.
The migration contains no drop/recreate or lossy conversion of existing media data, and applying it to StudyAIDb requires a separately approved controlled-maintenance action.
LessonResource supports Video, Image, Document, Link, and Attachment without requiring any lesson to have a resource.
Authenticated ContentAuthor users can perform only permitted draft management operations; reviewer/admin policy is required for verify, reject, publish, and unpublish transitions.
All mutating endpoints enforce RowVersion and return HTTP 409 for stale writes without losing either user's data.
Every management mutation and workflow transition produces a StaffAuditLog entry in the same successful transaction or causes the operation to fail.

URL validation accepts only the configured public http/https and provider policy and rejects javascript:, data:, file:, credentials, malformed URLs, private/reserved/loopback/link-local destinations, unsafe redirects, and disallowed providers or ports.
Learners receive only ordered, published, verified, non-archived resources for lessons they may access.
Lessons with no resources render normally with no placeholder media, fake URL, fabricated metadata, or false success state.
Invalid or unsupported video data does not crash or block LessonPage and is not rendered as a trusted playable resource.
Management UI covers loading, empty, validation, conflict, authorization, API failure, and confirmed-success states and remains usable at 390px.

Unit, isolated integration, and Playwright scenarios cover CRUD, reorder, archive, workflow, URL safety, optional media, invalid video, 401/403/409, refresh persistence, two-user isolation, API failure, and mobile layout.
P02 and P03 regression suites pass, or any unavailable/failing gate is recorded explicitly with logs and treated as unresolved.
No automated command, migration, fixture, test, bootstrap, seed, or browser run connects to or modifies StudyAIDb, StudyAIDb_E2E, or StudyAIDb_Dev.
database_safety_notes: ENV-01/ENV-02 are blocking constraints. StudyAIDb is never used by automated tests and receives no automatic migration, seed, bootstrap, import, reset, truncate, or drop operation. StudyAIDb_E2E and StudyAIDb_Dev are also forbidden. Integration and Playwright tests must resolve to a uniquely owned StudyAIDb_Clean_{GUID}, fail closed before connection when the name is absent or nonconforming, provision atomically with an ownership manifest, recover interrupted runs safely, and clean up only the exact owned database using bounded LOCK_TIMEOUT behavior—never SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE. Migration application to StudyAIDb requires explicit human approval, backup/rollback preparation, reviewed SQL, and controlled maintenance.
